subject: Request: Medline Health — volume-tier surcharge mitigation & tailored rate structure (exec sign-off needed)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T08:14:00-08:00
Subject: Request: Medline Health — volume-tier surcharge mitigation & tailored rate structure (exec sign-off needed)

Team — quick summary and ask up front: Medline is asking us to waive a new per-region surcharge they discovered in their procurement budget that would otherwise push them out of the committed tier. They want this waived for an initial 6 months, plus a restructure of the volume tiers so their committed ARR fits their FY27 budget. The account is strategic (enterprise health systems, multi-region) — this is an ask for a one-off commercial exception that requires VP/CFO sign-off.

Why this matters now:
- Customer: Medline Health (large systems integrator across 3 US regions).
- Ask: waive new-region surcharge for first 6 months + restructure committed tiers (move from 3 slabs down to 2, larger initial discount for first 12 months).
- Commercial rationale: preserves $1.2M ARR committed over 18 months vs losing the deal entirely; keeps Dedicated + Private deployment for them.

What I need from you:
- Kimberly: guidance on exec memo framing + final ask to present to finance.
- Marissa: high-level finance impact (ARR, margin delta) and whether we can structure an accelerated payment to offset P&L.
- Karthik: confirm this sits inside Sales guardrails or requires carveout.

Attached: Medline_rate_proposal_v3.pdf, financial_impact_model.csv (simple scenario P&L).

Quick numbers from my model (attached):
- Committed ARR (pro forma): $3.8M over 18 months if we accept restructure.
- Incremental expected margin hit (year 1): ~$140k — can be offset by 60-day prepayment option.
- Contingency: legal wants a shorter waiver window if we can require prepayment + clause to revert surcharge after month 6.

Proposed near-term approval: allow waiver through month 6 contingent on a 60-day prepayment for first 3 months or a one-time onboarding fee of $75k. If execs agree, I will send a formal counter to the customer tonight.

Thanks — this is time-sensitive (procurement needs final numbers by EOD Fri).

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachments: Medline_rate_proposal_v3.pdf (PDF), financial_impact_model.csv (CSV)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: Medline Health — volume-tier surcharge mitigation & tailored rate structure (exec sign-off needed)

Thanks Jonas — concise and helpful. A couple quick clarifying asks before I draft the exec memo:
1) Can you confirm if the surcharge is a third-party (carrier/ops) line item the customer added, or a Medline internal reclassification? That affects legal risk.
2) Please include the counterproposal language you plan to send if we get approval (I want the memo to contain an exact ask, fallback, and rollback clause).
3) Timeline: is EOD Fri firm? If yes we need a one-page executive summary for Marissa and a short redline for legal.

Initial position: I'm sympathetic to a short waiver window if it saves the committed ARR. Prefer limiting the full waiver to 3 months with an optional extension to 6 months if they meet payment milestones. Also prefer to require a $50k one-time onboarding/offset fee rather than prepay.

Karthik — flag if this is outside the commercial guardrails you track and whether we need VP-level exceptions.

If you can turn around a 1-paragraph proposed customer-facing sentence and a 1-line revenue mitigation item, I'll draft the memo and circulate for signoff.

— Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: Medline Health — volume-tier surcharge mitigation & tailored rate structure (exec sign-off needed)

Kim — per your notes below, attaching an exec memo (exec_memo_medline_v1.docx) and pasting the customer-facing counterproposal paragraph here for quick review.

Customer-facing counterproposal (for procurement):
"We appreciate the clarification on your internal chargebacks. Redwood can accommodate a temporary waiver of the new-region surcharge for an initial 3-month period, followed by an optional 3-month extension contingent on meeting the agreed committed usage milestones and a one-time implementation fee of $50,000. In parallel we are offering a revised volume-tier structure for the first 12 months to align with your FY27 budget; after month 12 the contract reverts to standard regional rates and the original tier ladder unless mutually renegotiated."

P&L mitigation (from attached model):
- Worst-case revenue delta (12-month): -$210k vs list.
- If they prepay first 3 months: delta becomes -$60k.
- If we require $50k implementation fee (preferred per Kim): delta becomes -$10k net over first year.

Legal flags included in memo: define waiver scope (only applies to region X surcharge line), require written acceptance within 72 hours, include immediate revert clause, and pre-approve rollback notification timeline.

If you and Marissa are aligned I'll send this to Lydia (Medline procurement) and request DocuSign for the amendment tonight.

— Jonas

Attachments: exec_memo_medline_v1.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: Medline Health — volume-tier surcharge mitigation & tailored rate structure (exec sign-off needed)

Appreciate the clear ask and the updated language. Finance view + recommendation below.

Summary: Based on the attached financial model, the preferred commercial-safe path that minimizes P&L exposure while preserving ARR is Kimberly's $50k implementation fee + 3-month waiver with a conditional 3-month extension tied to explicit usage milestones (we can define milestones in the amendment). This reduces downside to ~-$10k year-1 cash impact and keeps $3.8M committed ARR on the books.

Recommendation (for final signoff):
- Approve one-time waiver for first 3 months, extension to month 6 contingent on milestones.
- Require $50,000 implementation fee due within 30 days of amendment signing (or allow 60-day prepay option as Jonas described).
- Finance approves a one-time revenue reserve entry (reduction to achieved ARR) to be booked in FY26 close; legal to confirm amendment language for rollback.

I've completed the finance approval template and signed off (attached: finance_approval_template_signed.pdf). From finance perspective I recommend Marissa (me) sign the CFO approval on the final memo so the customer has an executive-signed document. Please send the final memo to me for signature.

Marissa Cole
